subject: Unexpected spike on June 30 — invoice hold & VAT treatment
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@clearstone.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 09:22:00 +0100
Subject: Unexpected June 30 invoice spike & automated collection hold

Hi Vanessa,

We woke up to an automated collection hold on our account and a charge for June 30 that is ~9x our usual token volume. I attached the invoice (clearstone_invoice_JUN2026.pdf) and a small slice of request logs we pulled (sample_requests_20260630.log).

Can you please:
- Confirm what triggered the spike (IP, API key, or ingestion job?)
- Hold any collections until we can reconcile — we have the transaction flagged on our side with finance
- Confirm VAT treatment for the adjustment if this was accidental (we are an EU entity)

This is blocking our payments team from approving the current invoice. Appreciate a quick breakdown and any evidence you can share.

Thanks,
Sarah
Payments & Ops
Clearstone Health
attachments: clearstone_invoice_JUN2026.pdf (pdf), sample_requests_20260630.log (text)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected June 30 invoice spike & automated collection hold

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I'm putting Ben and Kim on this thread to triage usage logs and collection status.\\n
Immediate updates:
- I have flagged collections for CL-9421 as "manual review" so our payment collector will not attempt an automatic retry today.
- Ben, can you pull the raw token attribution for 2026-06-30 and check API key / service-account alignment?
- Kim, please check tax/VAT handling rules for EU entity adjustments and what documentation we need to issue a retroactive credit.

Sarah — I should have a preliminary cause within 2 business hours. If it's an ingestion/backfill we can propose a provisional credit while we finish the audit.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

attachments: (none)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Clearstone (CL-9421) triage notes — large ingest attributed to prod key

Vanessa / Kim,

I pulled the per-request attribution for 2026-06-30 and attached the export (usage_export_20260630.csv) and a short token sample (token_sample.txt). Quick summary of findings:

- Volume: 9.4x baseline between 00:00–03:00 UTC on 2026-06-30.
- Attribution: 82% of the extra tokens are attributed to API key AK_live_8f4b (production), but the user-agent and source IPs match our historical ingestion cluster IP range (backfill cluster).
- Likely cause: a scheduled backfill job in Clearstone's infra used a production API key (service account rotation mismatch). The requests look like standard batch ingestion (multipart payloads, repeated identical prefix).
- No evidence of brute-force or malformed requests — traffic pattern strongly matches an internal ETL job.

Recommended next steps:
1) Offer a provisional customer credit equal to 60% of the overage while Clearstone confirms internal job config. Rationale: majority appears accidental but we keep a shared-responsibility buffer.
2) If Clearstone confirms a backfill with a non-prod ops error, convert provisional credit to full credit (100%) and issue an adjusted invoice.
3) Kimberly to confirm VAT reversal workflow and required supporting docs from Clearstone (signed statement, incident ticket id).

Attachments: usage_export_20260630.csv (csv), token_sample.txt (text)

Ben
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@clearstone.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, payments@clearstone.com
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 16:14:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected June 30 invoice spike & automated collection hold

Hi Sarah — quick update and proposed resolution.

Summary: our engineering team reviewed request attribution and traffic patterns for 2026-06-30 and believe the spike was caused by a Clearstone backfill/ETL job that used a production API key. We have not seen any malicious activity.

Proposal:
- Provisional credit: Redwood will issue a provisional credit equal to 60% of the overage amount on invoice JUN2026 as a stop-gap while Clearstone confirms the incident internally.
- Full adjustment: If Clearstone confirms the backfill and provides a short statement (one paragraph + incident ticket id), we will convert the provisional credit to a full 100% invoice adjustment and re-issue the corrected invoice.
- VAT handling: Kimberly — see below — will outline documentation we need for EU VAT reversal. Typically we require a signed customer statement + the original invoice id.

Next steps for Clearstone (requested):
1) Confirm whether the backfill ran using the prod API key AK_live_8f4b (or provide the actual key used).
2) If confirmed, send a one-paragraph statement and your internal ticket id.
3) Confirm whether you want Redwood to withhold collection until we finalize the credit (we currently have a manual hold in place).

Kimberly, can you paste the VAT reversal checklist in a follow-up?

Sarah — if you approve the provisional 60% credit I will provision it today and mark the invoice as "under adjustment" in billing; that will unblock payment processing on your end.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
